//: Realtime Database security rules for Suidoku 1v1.
Paste into Firebase console > Realtime Database > Rules, then Publish.
Kept in the repo so the rules are reviewable and versioned alongside the
transport that depends on them — the console is not a source of truth.
The app is unauthenticated (no Firebase Auth), so these rules cannot identify
who is who. They therefore constrain SHAPE and SIZE rather than identity:
anyone can write, but only well-formed, small, short-lived records. Message
authenticity is checked a second time on the client in battleValidation.js —
roomId and senderId must match the room the player is actually in.
GOTCHA, learned the hard way: a bare "$other": { ".validate": false } does
NOT mean 'any child other than the named ones'. The wildcard matches EVERY
child, so it rejected playerId/level/timestamp too and every queue write
failed with PERMISSION_DENIED. Each allowed field must be named explicitly
alongside it, which is what the entries below do.
This is deliberate for a closed test. Before a wider release, add Firebase
Anonymous Auth and tighten '.write' to "auth != null", so a bot cannot flood
the queue. Do NOT relax these to ".read": true, ".write": true — that is an
open database anyone on the internet can wipe or fill.
